schema.rationale: The reusable distinction is between an operative authorization and a recipient merely appearing in a definition, recital, prohibition, or safeguard. Intrinsic qualifications such as need-to-know, purpose limitation, and existing confidentiality duties preserve an authorization, whereas a requirement to obtain new discloser consent does not itself authorize disclosure. A specific third-party restriction controls over a broader clause with a vague purpose exception. This refined schema also captures general internal-sharing authority without treating defined Representatives as automatically permitted recipients.
schema.read_question: Read the complete agreement independently of any hypothesis. Identify the role classes that an operative clause affirmatively authorizes to receive or access Confidential Information, resolving definitions only when an operative authorization actually incorporates them. Also identify operative employee or third-party nondisclosure restrictions and their exception relationship. Preserve permissions subject to intrinsic need-to-know, purpose, or pre-existing confidentiality qualifications; distinguish those qualifications from a requirement to obtain new consent. Exclude bare recipient mentions, information descriptions, recitals, and duties that do not establish permission. Use the most specific audience rule where clauses overlap, and do not transfer safeguards or recipient classes from another agreement.

source_fields.name: operative_disclosure_recipient_classes
source_fields.question: Which recipient classes are affirmatively covered by an operative voluntary disclosure, access, or internal-sharing authorization? Include a class incorporated coherently by safeguards attached to the authorized recipients. Exclude classes found only in definitions, recitals, prohibitions, or bare mentions. Use internal_personnel_unspecified for an express general internal-sharing authorization. Use none_explicit only when the complete source supports that no recipient class is operatively authorized.

source_fields.name: ordinary_disclosure_restriction_relations
source_fields.question: What operative restrictions govern ordinary voluntary disclosure to employees or third parties when they are not otherwise affirmatively authorized? A requirement for newly obtained consent or permission is a restriction, not present authorization. Record an independent-purpose exception only when it genuinely qualifies the applicable audience restriction; a generic purpose exception does not override a separate, more specific third-party consent rule. Do not infer an employee-specific prohibition from generic references to another person unless employees are expressly within that restriction. Use none_determinative only after reviewing the complete source.
